chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Halbi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the expiation for an oath, he should feed ten poor people; for each poor person, a mud of wheat or a mud of flour and a handful, or their clothing, for each person two garments, or freeing a slave. He has the choice among these three; whichever of the three he does. If he is unable to do any one of the three, then fasting is upon him for three days.

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What are the options for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the hierarchical expiation for breaking an oath, prioritizing material charity (feeding or clothing ten poor people) or manumission, with fasting as a tertiary fallback. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, emphasizing accessibility by allowing the least burdensome option that the individual can afford, thereby ensuring the expiation is achievable for all socioeconomic classes.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, both together from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘With regards to an expiation for the oath, he should feed ten poor ones, for each poor, a handful from wheat, or a handful from flour; or their clothing, for each human being, two clothes; or freeing of a neck (slave); and he would be with the choice in that, whichever of the three he does. So if he is unable over (even) one from the three, so the Fasting is upon him, for three days’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash ‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘if has narrated from al-Fadf ibn Shadhan from all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “About the case of Kaffarah (expiation) because of oath abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It (expiation) is to feed ten destitute people each with one mud (a certain measurement) or a handful of wheat or flour, or clothe them with two pieces of clothes to each person, or free a slave. He has the choice for any one of the three that he may choose and if he cannot do anyone of them then he must fast for three days.’”
